These antibiotics work by inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis, leading to cell lysis. While beta-lactam antibiotics can cause various side effects, gastrointestinal hemorrhage is not commonly associated with them. More common side effects include allergic reactions, gastrointestinal upset, and superinfections due to disruption of the normal gut flora. Therefore, the plausibility of gastrointestinal hemorrhage as a side effect of a beta-lactam antibiotic is LOW.
